item.title: Version 2.2.0
item.description:
## App Updates
### Added
- Added system-network support for private IP address ranges used by local model services, while retaining public-network transport protections. - MacTools can open its panel below the Dynamic Island and restores its menu-bar icon when the hover plugin is disabled or no compatible display is connected. - Open installed or running applications directly by voice without assigning hotkeys. Asking for an already active app keeps it visible. - Control enabled plugins by voice with native approvals and microphone permission guidance. Conversations survive plugin refreshes, while stopped or expired sessions cannot start waiting commands.
### Changed
- Plugin Sets now open inside Settings and finish with clear tips for using and configuring plugins. Refined previews use each component’s default panel while preserving existing layouts. - Import now clarifies that selecting Shortcuts resets omitted bindings to defaults. Unselected categories and local data are preserved. - Empty panels now link to plugin installation when no plugins are installed, or directly to panel editing when plugins are available, replacing the tool-pack shortcut.
### Fixed
- Preferences Backup now shows plugin coverage, exclusions, and restore results. Failed exports preserve the last good automatic or cloud backup, and dependent shortcuts follow successfully included definitions. - Imported prompt shortcuts apply only when their template definitions restore successfully. - Panel editing keeps navigation centered, places Panel Width after Add Widgets, and removes redundant drag controls.
## Plugin Updates
### Added
- Translator now accepts private IPv4 and IPv6 HTTP endpoints, preserves custom endpoint paths, and restricts redirects to the configured service. Requires MacTools 2.2.0 or later. - The Apple Container card now shows live CPU, memory, and disk usage. Containers gain a configuration window with CPU, memory, and disk I/O charts plus terminal access, and machines can open a terminal too. - New Dynamic Island Hover Panel plugin opens MacTools from the Dynamic Island. The main menu-bar icon stays visible by default, with an option to hide it; saved visibility preferences are preserved. - Change automatic access for new plugins by voice, with confirmation before enabling. Changes affect future conversations, and stopping cancels pending changes. - New Voice Assistant offers a persistent panel with live captions, audio meters, and global shortcuts. Keys stay in Keychain; feature access supports search, batch changes, and cancelable edits. - Voice Assistant ends idle conversations after a configurable timeout, defaulting to one minute. Replies and tasks finish before the timer starts, and the floating panel stays open. - Voice Assistant can wait for speech on your Mac before connecting, preserving your opening words while reducing unused API time. Connect when I speak is enabled by default and can be changed in settings. - Choose whether newly installed plugins are automatically available from the main Voice Assistant settings page. Automatic access is on by default; current choices are kept when switching to manual approval. - Voice Assistant groups connection, conversation, and feature access settings. Model and pricing details explain billed connected silence and free local speech detection, with official links and speaker troubleshooting. - Ask for fresh brightness, system, power, appearance, Keep Awake, Night Shift, and mute status. Brightness commands verify their target and distinguish hardware readings from software dimming without undoing adjustments. - Voice Assistant reports audible speech and session usage, recovers from interrupted connections, and immediately stops recording and feature access when stopped.
### Changed
- Power Status collapses high-energy apps by default and samples only while expanded. The battery bar is easier to read, and power flow rows show draw without repeating wattage in the header.
### Fixed
- Backups now include more plugin settings, custom layouts, and stable app mappings. Private prompt text and launch-item notes require a separate opt-in; local data and permissions stay on your Mac. - Fixed upside-down app icons in Launchpad folder previews, including when dragging a folder. - Per-app keyboard modes now reliably switch the top row back to the Mac shortcuts or F1–F12 mode when apps change, after waking the Mac, or when a system write briefly fails. - AI settings transfer preserves verified local credentials and excluded private text, including large prompts and legacy Translator keys. Imported services need local key setup before accessing saved credentials. - Importing Clipboard preferences preserves local history across app restarts. - AI Assistant and Translator back up saved disabled service drafts without requiring complete settings. Drafts stay disabled after import. - Imports preserve unrelated prompt and Launch Control drafts, restored input rules, and included prompt shortcuts. AI prompt edits wait for recovery to finish, and Translator rejects unusable restored services. - Imported app volumes affect new playback while current playback keeps its gain; later edits preserve other live routes. Usage refresh intervals and low-battery warnings resume with restored settings and permission. - Clipboard History creates separate snippets when using New Snippet repeatedly, preserving previously saved snippets.
### Security
- Voice Assistant discards muted and outdated buffered audio, and delayed failures from an old connection no longer stop a new conversation.
